items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: And I played, uh, I was playing banjo. And T-Boy Remy was playing trumpet. And, uh, uh, uh, what did we ever had on the drum? Uh, uh, I believe we had Erich Begau on the drum. Same show.

ctx.x: What about, uh, Tranchinas and, and the, uh, Tokyo Gardens and all those places in Spanish Fork? Were you ever out there?

Uh, no. Uh, only Tranchini that had a place where we played at with, uh, with, uh, Mumford ourselves. Uh, um, uh, Uh, let's see. Uh, he's king to the Mumford's too. He's a piano player. And, uh, the Tranchini had, he had a, he had a, all of them there at the corner of Claiborne and, and Tulane Avenue. Uh-huh. That was a nice spot there, but that was only for the weekend. Uh, Leon Mumford. Leon Mumford played trombone, uh, piano. Uh-huh. And I played, uh, I was playing banjo. And T-Boy Remy was playing trumpet.…

Did you, did you know Henry Ponce? Ponce. Henry Ponce. He had a joint near Segretas. They had a little fight going. items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: He had T-Boy Remy with him.

ctx.x: Well, uh, they'd have six pieces. We went to the Junk Hotel and played there. Well, he had Son Thomas playing guitar. I was playing bass. He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets. He had T-Boy Remy with him. And he had a fella called Pill on the clarinet. He died. He had a little bow-legged fella called Pill. Well, after that, well, Louis played around spot jobs around different places. And then, that's when he went up the line. Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a…
And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?
